channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Why Pool Depth Changes the Price of Your Swap
item.description: A deeper pool usually gives a swap a smaller price impact because the trade uses less of its available liquidity, though fees and slippage still affect the final result.

item.title: What an Avalanche Swap Costs Beyond the Pool Fee
item.description: An Avalanche swap can cost more than its pool fee: network gas, approvals and price impact affect what you spend and receive, and costs change with timing.

item.title: How Voter Bribes Compete With DEX Fee Rewards
item.description: Vote bribes pay governance voters to steer token emissions, while DEX fees reward trading activity; the better return depends on timing, pool demand and token value.

item.title: How to Swap Into WETH Before Funding a Pool
item.description: Swap into WETH by wrapping ETH or trading for it, then match the pool’s network, token pair and funding rules before you approve a deposit in your wallet.

item.title: What a Sequencer Outage Means for Treasury Swaps
item.description: A sequencer outage can leave treasury swaps pending or delayed; check chain status, transaction state, nonce and quote expiry before retrying on an L2.

item.title: How to Set Slippage for Token Swaps on Base
item.description: On Base, slippage sets the worst output a swap can accept; use the app’s estimate, check minimum received, and raise the limit only when a cause calls for it.

item.title: Why Chain Maintenance Can Hide Transfer Routes
item.description: Chain maintenance can hide transfer routes when a network or bridge pauses; check whether the route is unavailable now or unsupported before changing your plan.

item.title: Send cross-chain deposits with expiry time in hand
item.description: Send a cross-chain deposit only after checking the route, fee and expiry, then leave enough time for the source chain to confirm it before the channel closes.

item.title: How Swap Proceeds Can Pay for a Contract Call
item.description: A swap can do more than deliver tokens: Chainflip can send the output to a supported contract and call it, if the message and gas budget are set up correctly.

item.title: Check a Cross-Chain Swap Before You Send
item.description: A cross-chain swap can send value to the wrong network or address if its route is misread. Check the assets, minimum output, fees and destination before signing.

item.title: How to size recurring Solana treasury swaps
item.description: Recurring Solana treasury swaps work best as a policy for converting a defined share of inflows, with size tied to cash needs, liquidity and execution cost.

item.title: Why a cross-chain refund can take hours
item.description: Cross-chain refunds can take hours because a failed destination leg may need confirmation, route checks and a separate return transaction. Here is what to check before retrying.

item.title: Why a bridged token can have a different name
item.description: A bridged token may carry a new name because each chain needs its own token record; the label can show its origin, bridge or wrapped status.

item.title: Why Bridge Relayers Charge an Extra Execution Fee
item.description: A bridge relayer fee pays for the destination-chain transaction and the service that submits it. Learn what it covers, why quotes change, and how to compare routes.

item.title: How to Check Your First Mantle Bridge Deposit
item.description: After your first Mantle deposit, match the Ethereum transaction to the Mantle-side transfer, then check the destination wallet and token before retrying.

item.title: Why a Crypto Bridge Transfer Stays Pending
item.description: A pending bridge transfer means the move has started but may still need source-chain confirmation, proof delivery or destination execution before funds arrive.

item.title: How to Read a BSC Wallet’s Token Activity
item.description: A BSC wallet’s token history separates transfers, contract calls and approvals, helping you trace what changed and judge what a chart leaves out.

item.title: Treasury Teams Should Review Token Approvals Before Bridging
item.description: A bridge approval lets a contract spend tokens; treasury teams can reduce risk by checking the spender, setting a limited amount and reviewing leftover access.

item.title: Check the receiving network before sending crypto
item.description: A crypto address works only when the receiving wallet or service supports the network carrying the asset, so check the network before you send funds.

item.title: Why a Polygon PoS Withdrawal Can Stall
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal can pause at a checkpoint or claim step; check the transaction stage, wallet network and gas before retrying, since each stage has a different cause and next step.
